title: Governor Abbott appoints Ripley and names West chair of Teacher Retirement System board

Governor Abbott appoints Ripley and names West chair of Teacher Retirement System board
Governor Greg Abbott appointed Clayton Ripley to serve on the Teacher Retirement System Board until August 2031 while naming Dan West as chair. Both bring extensive experience from business leadership roles across Texas industries.
Governor Greg Abbott appointed Clayton Ripley to the Teacher Retirement System of Texas Board of Trustees for a term set to expire on August 31, 2031, and named Dan West as chair of the Board, according to a Sept. 21 announcement. The Teacher Retirement System Board manages retirement and other benefits for teachers and employees of the state’s public schools and institutions of higher education.
Clayton Ripley is vice president of Holt Aerial, which succeeded TGM Wind Services after its acquisition by Holt Cat in 2021. He is also founder and managing director of several Texas-based businesses, including Town Lake Capital Management, an investment advisory firm regulated by the Texas State Securities Board, and BGCP Holdings, a real estate development company. Ripley holds a CPA license in good standing with the Texas State Board of Public Accountancy and is a member at large with the Texas Society of CPAs. He serves as treasurer for the Texas Land Trust Council and is involved with All Saints Presbyterian Church. Currently, he serves as a gubernatorial appointee on the Texas Appraiser Licensing and Certification Board. Ripley earned his Bachelor of Business Administration from Baylor University.
Dan West is an investor at SCF Partners, which works with energy services, equipment, and technology companies. He belongs to the State Bar of Texas as well as its Oil, Gas, and Energy Resources Law Section. West also chairs Brillante Academy's board; sits on the board for Sam Houston Area Council of Scouting America; participates in the International & National Security Law Executive Committee for the Federalist Society; and has served since 2022 as a gubernatorial appointee on the Economic Incentive Oversight Board. His educational background includes degrees from Harvard College (Bachelor’s in Economics), Harvard Business School (MBA), and Harvard Law School (Juris Doctor). West previously served in infantry operations with the U.S. Marine Corps in Afghanistan and during NATO's Libyan intervention before receiving an honorable discharge at Captain rank in 2013.
The Governor’s office provides leadership across economic opportunity initiatives while supporting cultural understanding through commissions that advance opportunities for women and people with disabilities; it also promotes education policy statewide, according to the official website. The office operates out of The Governor's Mansion—a Greek Revival structure serving since 1856—which stands among America's oldest continuously occupied governor's residences.
